items.headline: Pittsburgh receives $3 million for Boulevard of the Allies renovation
items.summary: The City of Pittsburgh will receive $3 million from the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation to renovate the Boulevard of the Allies in the Central Business District. The city's Department of Mobility and Infrastructure plans a tree-lined median connecting Grant Street to Stanwix Street and Point State Park.

items.headline: Maricopa County Eviction Prevention Pilot Launches, Serves High-Risk Communities
items.summary: Maricopa County launched an Eviction Prevention Pilot Program formally approved by its Board of Supervisors. The program offers eligible households up to $3,200 for as much as two months of rent arrears and partners with the City of Phoenix for utility assistance and case management.

items.headline: City of Cleveland launches Rave emergency notification system
items.summary: Cleveland launched Rave, its official emergency notification system for alerts to residents, businesses, visitors and neighboring areas during emergencies and major events. The system supports text, email and voice notifications with configurable geographic and topic preferences.

items.headline: More than 500 possible heat-related deaths under investigation in Maricopa County
items.summary: More than 500 possible heat-related deaths are under investigation in Maricopa County this summer, exceeding the number of heat-related deaths confirmed in the county last year. Phoenix firefighters and Banner Health clinicians reported an accompanying surge in heat-related calls and emergency-room cases.

items.headline: NCDHHS urges families to keep children current on vaccines before school
items.summary: The North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services urged families to ensure children and teens are current on required and recommended vaccinations as students return to school. The department said North Carolina does not anticipate changes to its clinical guidance following an Aug. 10 federal executive order.
items.entityName: North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services
items.source: North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services

items.headline: JobsOhio supports 50 new L3Harris positions in Southwest Ohio
items.summary: JobsOhio said it is partnering with L3Harris Technologies and REDI Cincinnati on a talent strategy supporting 50 new positions at L3Harris's Cincinnati location. The roles span engineering, operations, program management and finance as the company scales output for military customers.

items.headline: Ohio House lawmakers propose sweeping data-center regulation bill
items.summary: Ohio House legislators introduced House Bill 983, which would require voter approval for certain data-center construction or expansion, add air and water standards, bar local tax incentives for data centers and require disclosure of development agreements. The proposal would also assign owners responsibility for certain water-supply and pressure impacts.

items.headline: Ohio attorney general candidate seeks investigation involving JobsOhio and Intel
items.summary: Ohio Democratic attorney general nominee John Kulewicz called for the state inspector general to investigate reported ties among JobsOhio's board chair, the governor's office and Intel. The report said JobsOhio was created by the General Assembly and its board is appointed by the governor; JobsOhio said it has been transparent and free of conflicts.

items.headline: Ohio joins $15.5 million settlement with NewRez over force-placed insurance
items.summary: The Ohio Department of Commerce Division of Financial Institutions joined 47 other state financial agencies in a $15.5 million settlement with mortgage servicer NewRez. The settlement covers force-placed insurance costs imposed on borrowers with active homeowners policies and includes borrower refunds, costs and penalties, plus enhanced monitoring requirements.

items.headline: Ohio House bill would increase penalties for coordinated retail theft
items.summary: House Bill 615, under consideration in the Ohio Statehouse, would create a new group-retail-theft offense with penalties that rise based on the number of participants and value stolen. The bill has received two hearings in the Small Business Committee.

items.headline: NYITCOM and UA Little Rock launch medical-school pathway
items.summary: The New York Institute of Technology College of Osteopathic Medicine at Arkansas State University announced a partnership with the University of Arkansas at Little Rock. The pathway will admit up to 10 students through a joint process, with the program expected to begin in spring 2027.

items.headline: New York launches Lead Rental Registry information sessions in Broome County
items.summary: The Broome County Health Department announced information sessions for a new Lead Rental Registry launched by the New York State Department of Health. The program covers qualifying older two-or-more-unit properties in two Binghamton ZIP codes, with inspections required every three years and lead hazards subject to correction.
items.entityName: New York State Department of Health

items.headline: Former Bio Family Clinic employees seek pay and unemployment benefits after closure
items.summary: Former employees of Yuma's Bio Family Clinic said they remain mostly unpaid and unable to collect unemployment after the clinic closed following the doctor's arrest. The case alleges that the clinic defrauded the Arizona Health Care Cost Containment System out of millions of dollars; AHCCCS is Arizona's Medicaid agency.
items.entityName: Arizona Health Care Cost Containment System

items.headline: Ohio lawmakers push limits on Flock license-plate cameras
items.summary: A bipartisan group of Ohio lawmakers is considering new limits on Flock Safety license-plate cameras. One proposal would prohibit Flock cameras and other AI-assisted surveillance technologies statewide, while another would impose financial restrictions on communities that use them.

items.headline: Ohio University to update Concur travel booking system
items.summary: Ohio University said its Concur travel-booking experience will change later this month as its travel-management partner upgrades the airfare, hotel, rental-car and rail content system. The migration is scheduled for Aug. 21 and may temporarily make Concur unavailable.

items.headline: PennDOT schedules I-279-to-Fort Duquesne Bridge inspection in Pittsburgh
items.summary: PennDOT announced inspection work on southbound I-279 to the Fort Duquesne Bridge in Pittsburgh. A single-lane restriction was scheduled from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. on Aug. 18, weather permitting.

items.headline: Worcester Green Tech Park's first prospective tenant enters permitting
items.summary: The Worcester Business Development Corporation said the first prospective commercial tenant for Worcester's Green Tech Park is in the permitting process. The project also has a recently announced $12.8 million infrastructure grant, and the prospective tenant would occupy a 50,000-square-foot building and employ about 55 people.

quality.notes: Searched all 108 unique canonical names. Verified official pages where available and otherwise used reliable local/state reporting; syndicated vaccine reports were consolidated. Generic sector commentary, jobs pages, stale/undated pages, inaccessible paywalled pages, weak geographic matches, and unsupported snippets were excluded. Date-only publication pages are retained only where the page clearly identifies the Aug. 17 or Aug. 18, 2026 publication day within the window.
